We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction (level 2). The target SMILES is a complex molecule: an alkene attached to aromatic ring and a cyclopentanol with CF3 group? Actually CF3 attached to carbon 15. The description hints carbonyl-ene reaction forward: carbonyl + alkene -> new C-C bond, hydroxyl, five-membered ring formed. So retrosynthetic step is reverse of carbonyl-ene: break C-O bond (hydroxyl) and break C-C bond forming ring, generate a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene (maybe exocyclic). So we need to find a template that does carbonyl-ene reverse. The search gave template 1229769 etc. The first template seems to be a carbonyl-ene? It shows retro_smarts_template: '[C:5]-[C@;H0;D4;+0:6](-[C:7])(-[OH;D1;+0:8])-[C;H0;D4;+0:1](-[F;D1;H0:2])(-[F;D1;H0:3])-[F;D1;H0:4]>>C-[Si](-C)(-C)-[C;H0;D4;+0:1](-[F;D1;H0:2])(-[F;D1;H0:3])-[F;D1;H0:4].[C:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](-[C:7])=[O;H0;D1;+0:8]'

That seems to be a carbonyl-ene where product is the cyclic alcohol with CF3 and a silyl group? Actually the product side is the target? The retro template shows product (right side) is the cyclic alcohol with CF3 and also a silyl group? Wait the retro_smarts_template is left side (reactants) -> right side (product). It shows left side: [C:5]-[C@...]-[C...CF3] (the cyclic alcohol) and [C:5]-[C...]=O (a ketone). So the forward reaction (retro) is a carbonyl-ene: a ketone + alkene -> cyclic alcohol + silyl? Actually there is a silyl group on the carbonyl side. Might be a protecting group.

But we just need any template that matches our target. We can try to check matching with template ID 1229769. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching.
